text: Working on it: `Interval.fromISO` in src/interval.js doesn't honor `Settings.throwOnInvalid`, so invalid input returns an invalid Interval instead of throwing `InvalidArgumentError`. I have a subagent fixing it and running the interval test suite; ETA ~10 min.

It returns `NaN`. `parseDigits` first tries `parseInt(str, 10)`; if that's `NaN` it builds a string from the non-Latin digit systems (`value = ""` initially) and then returns `parseInt(value, 10)`. With no parseable digits, `value` stays `""`, and `parseInt("", 10)` is `NaN` — so the function returns `NaN` (not `0` or `""`).

It returns the pair `[null, {}]` — i.e. an array whose first element is the failed `String.prototype.match` result (`null`) and whose second element is an empty object. (On a successful match it returns `[matches, all]` with the captured groups and the deserialized token values.)
Got it — a second subagent is on the `src/impl/util.js` bug (DateTime#plus across the year-100 barrier through February). ETA ~12 min for that one; the interval.js fix is still in progress.

It returns an error object, not `false`: `validYear` is `false`, so the function returns `unitOutOfRange("weekYear", obj.weekYear)`, which is an `InvalidUnitError` (an `Error` subclass from src/errors.js) with message like `Invalid unit weekYear: <value>`. `false` is only returned when all three checks pass.

`latn` (Latin/Western digits). `digitRegex` builds the regex from `numberingSystems[numberingSystem || "latn"]`, and `latn` maps to `\\d`, i.e. `[0-9]`.

#4 fixed and verified. Cause: `objToLocalTS` in src/impl/util.js reverted the 1900-shifted year with `setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`, which kept the month/day that JS had already normalized in the 19xx year (e.g. year 2000, a leap year) — so `0099-12-31 + 2 months + 2 days` gave 0100-03-01 instead of 0100-03-02. Fix: `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)` so normalization happens in the correct year. Only affects 0 <= year < 100. Test suite: 892 passed / 2 failed, identical to the pre-fix baseline (the 2 failures are pre-existing ICU-related French `FFF`/`FFFF` expectations in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js).

It sets the internal `defaultZone` variable to `null` (it does not throw). So the `defaultZone` getter then falls back to `LocalZone.instance`.

`Zone` is an abstract interface class, and its `type` getter is abstract: it just throws `new ZoneIsAbstractError()` (message: "Zone is an abstract class"). Concrete subclasses (`LocalZone`, `IANAZone`, `FixedOffsetZone`, `InvalidZone`) override it to return their own type string, e.g. `"local"`, `"iana"`, `"fixed"`, `"invalid"`.

A `FixedOffsetZone` built from that value: `zone = new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)` (where `matches.Z` is the parsed numeric offset in minutes). That zone is returned as the second element of the `[vals, zone]` pair; the other branches give `IANAZone.create(matches.z)` when only `matches.z` is defined, and `null` when neither is.

#8 fixed and verified. Cause: `DateTime#isInDST` used `this.set({ month: 1 }).offset` as the standard-time reference, but `set({month:1})` keeps the day-of-month, so for a January date the "reference" was the same instant — still in DST during the 1974 US year-round DST period, making isInDST false. Fix in src/datetime.js: compare against `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 }).offset`. Verified: all 294 days 1974-01-06..1974-10-26 are isInDST true in America/New_York and America/Los_Angeles, 1974-10-28/1975-01-15 false, and normal years (2016 winter/summer, Sydney) unchanged. Full suite: 892 passed / 2 failed, same as baseline.
Started a sixth subagent on the `src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js` bug (invalid zone for non-numeric offsets). ETA ~12 min. #1, #11 and #15 are still in progress.

#11 fixed and verified. Cause: the conversion matrices in src/duration.js were missing entries, so conversions involving `quarters` silently gave 0/NaN. Fix: added `quarters: 4` to `casualMatrix.years` and `accurateMatrix.years`, and `seconds: 91*24*60*60` to `casualMatrix.quarters`. All 72 unit pairs now normalize/convert consistently (checked with both casual and longterm accuracies); full suite 892 passed / 2 failed, same as baseline.
`hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0` — i.e. hour 24 is allowed only as exactly midnight (00:00:00.000), alongside the normal `integerBetween(hour, 0, 23)` check.

#15 fixed and verified. Cause: `padStart` in src/impl/util.js padded by slicing the whole signed number, so the minus sign was swallowed into the padding (`padStart(-1, 4)` → `"00-1"`), making `toISODate()` render negative years as `00-1-01-01`. Fix: emit the sign separately and pad the magnitude (`-1` → `-0001`). Verified: -1 → `-0001-01-01`, -50 → `-0050-01-01`, -1234 → `-1234-01-01`, positive years unchanged; full suite 892 passed / 2 failed, same as baseline.
Per the abstract docstring in src/zone.js: `'narrow'`, `'short'`, or `'techie'` — returning e.g. `'+6'`, `'+06:00'`, or `'+0600'` respectively.
